steps.title: The Opening Question
steps.content:
So {{contact_first_name}}, how have things been since {{pt_you}} got {{pt_your}} braces off with us? Are the teeth still holding straight and {{pt_they_are}} happy with the smile, have you noticed a little shifting starting to creep in, or {{pt_moved_back_q}}?

(This question has only three possible answers. Click the one you hear.)

steps.title: Still Holding Straight: Celebrate the Win
steps.content:
I love hearing that, {{contact_first_name}}, after all that time in braces, a straight smile that STAYS straight is the whole goal, and it means the retainer is doing exactly what it’s supposed to do.

(Celebrate genuinely. This is {{pt_your}} win. Then ask permission for the questions.)

steps.title: Some Shifting: Normalize, Then Update the File
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, that’s completely normal. Teeth naturally want to drift back toward where they started, especially once the retainer routine slips; {{pt_no_fault}}, and it’s exactly why we check in. The good news is that when shifting is caught early, it’s usually much easier to correct.

What do you think made it start creeping back? Was it the retainers wearing out, the retainers just not getting worn as much, or something else?

(Let them answer. Do NOT try to book yet.)

steps.title: Moved Back Quite a Bit: Normalize, Then Update the File
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, that’s completely normal. Teeth naturally want to drift back toward where they started once the retainer routine slips; {{pt_no_fault}}, and it’s exactly why we check in. I remember how great that smile looked the day the braces came off, {{pt_proud}}.

What do you think made it come back? Was it the retainers wearing out, the retainers just not getting worn as much, or something else?

(Let them answer. Do NOT try to book yet. Be warm and non-judgmental.)

steps.title: Ask Permission for the Questions
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, since I have you on the phone and I’m updating {{pt_your_file}} anyway, I’d like to ask you a few quick questions about how {{pt_smile_bite}} are holding up. Teeth move so slowly you never catch them doing it, which is exactly why these questions matter. Is that okay?

(Wait for the yes. Almost everyone says yes. You asked permission, and it’s their file.)

steps.title: The Transition: Acknowledge and Ask Permission
steps.content:
Now {{contact_first_name}}, obviously I know you’ve told me what’s been going on, and we’re absolutely going to talk about that. But while I have you on the phone, I’d like to ask you a few additional questions so we get {{pt_your_file}} completely up to date. Is that okay?

(Wait for the yes before starting the questions.)

steps.title: The Questions: Update the File
The Questions: Update the File
Making It Real
steps.content:
(Take the concern they named and make it present with three questions, in order.)

{{pt_mir_q1}}? Since we last saw {{pt_them}}, or longer?

{{pt_mir_q2}}?

{{pt_mir_q3}}? (Let them open up. Do not rush.)

Then respond with empathy: Thank you for sharing that, it makes complete sense, and that is exactly the kind of thing {{rec_pronoun}} help people with every single day.

steps.title: The Review & Bridge to Emotion
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, let me make sure I've got this right. (Recap what they told you: how long, how often, how it affects them.) Did I get that right?

And it sounds like {{pt_bridge_q}}. Is that fair to say?

(About 95% say yes. That yes is the moment.)

steps.title: The Magic Question & Recommendation
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, a quick check lets {{rec_pronoun}} see exactly where the teeth stand compared to the day the braces came off. If it’s minor, often a refreshed retainer or a short touch-up is all it takes to get things back on track, and if everything’s holding better than you think, {{rec_pronoun}}’ll tell you that too, because the last thing {{rec_pronoun}} want to do is waste your time or your money. Does that make sense?

(Wait for the yes.)

{{contact_first_name}}, can I make a recommendation?

(Wait for yes.)

Based on everything you’ve told me, my recommendation is that we {{pt_get_you_in}} for that quick check. Does that sound reasonable?

(Ask “does that sound reasonable”, never “does that sound good.” Click what you hear next.)

steps.title: They Hesitate: Uncover Why
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, help me understand. What's holding you back from letting us {{pt_get_you_in}} to take a look? Is it the timing, or is there something else on your mind?

(Ask this easygoing and curious, not pushy. You're simply trying to understand what's getting in the way so you can help. Then stop and let them tell you.)

What are your thoughts about that?

steps.title: Nothing Found: The Retainer Check
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, I’m glad everything else is in good shape, and we’re thrilled to hear it.

Let me ask you one last thing. How are the retainers holding up? Still going in at night, or has that kind of fallen out of the routine?

(Let them answer. No judgment either way. Retainer habits slip, and retainers themselves stretch and wear out over time.)

{{contact_first_name}}, even when everything feels like it’s holding, retainers age. They stretch, warp, and wear thin, and teeth will quietly take advantage of that. The easiest way to protect everything those braces accomplished is a quick check: we make sure everything is actually holding where it should, and if the retainers need refreshing we handle it right there. Does that make sense?

(Wait for the yes.)

{{contact_first_name}}, can I make a recommendation?

(Wait for the yes.)

Let’s {{pt_get_you_in}} so we can check those retainers, and that smile stays exactly where it belongs. Does that sound reasonable?

steps.title: Parent Mode
steps.content: (Parent mode is on, every screen from here uses parent/guardian wording automatically.)

steps.title: Objection: Braces again?
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, that’s the number one thing people worry about, and here’s the honest answer: usually not. When shifting is caught reasonably early, it’s often a much smaller fix. A refreshed retainer or a short touch-up, not a whole new set of braces. The check tells us exactly where things stand, and that’s the point of coming in: you’ll know precisely what it would take before deciding anything.

(Do NOT quote specific prices or promise treatment lengths on the call. The exam determines that.)

Confirm and continue: Does that make sense? (Wait for the yes.) Okay, let’s find you a time. I have (day) at (time) or (day) at (time). Which is better for you?

steps.title: Objection: How long would fixing it take?
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, it depends entirely on how far things have moved, which is exactly why the quick check comes first. What I can tell you is that catching movement early almost always means a shorter, simpler fix than waiting, and after the check you’ll know exactly what your situation would take, no guessing.

Confirm and continue: Does that make sense? (Wait for the yes.) Okay, let’s find you a time. I have (day) at (time) or (day) at (time). Which is better for you?

steps.title: Objection: The retainer routine slipped
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, please don’t be. There’s truly no judgment here. Teeth naturally want to drift back toward where they started the moment the retainer routine slips. That’s just how teeth behave, and {{pt_no_fault}}. It’s exactly why we check in. I remember how great that smile looked when the braces came off, and we’d simply love to help {{pt_them}} protect it.

Confirm and continue: Does that make sense? (Wait for the yes.) Okay, let’s find you a time. I have (day) at (time) or (day) at (time). Which is better for you?

steps.title: Objection: I need to think about it
steps.content:
That's completely fair, {{contact_first_name}}. Can I ask what part you'd want to think over? Sometimes it's the cost, sometimes the timing, and sometimes people just want to be sure it's the right move, which one is closest for you?

(Listen, their answer usually points to one of the other buttons below. If it stays general, keep going.)

The nice thing is, coming in is really just information. You'd find out exactly what the options look like and what it would involve, and then you get to make the decision with real answers instead of wondering. And if it's not the right fit, we'll tell you that too.

Confirm and continue: Does that make sense? (Wait for a fast yes.) Do you have any other questions or concerns?

steps.title: Objection: Just send me information
steps.content:
I'd be glad to get you some information, {{contact_first_name}}. The one thing I'd say is that a link or a flyer can only tell you so much. It can't look at your specific situation. That's really what the visit is for: you find out exactly what the options look like for you and get answers that apply to you. So let me get you on the schedule first, and you'll have real answers to go on.

Confirm and continue: Does that make sense? (Wait for a fast yes.) Do you have any other questions or concerns?
